item-080.title: Conservation Corps Minnesota & Iowa — Individual Placements
item-080.deadline: Rolling — new positions posted continuously at conservationcorps.org/join
item-080.body: Conservation Corps MN & IA places AmeriCorps members with Soil and Water Conservation Districts and natural resource agencies. Wetland inventories, water quality monitoring, GIS mapping, species surveys. Full-year IPs and summer positions. New positions roll continuously.
item-080.desc: Conservation Corps Minnesota & Iowa places AmeriCorps members with Soil and Water Conservation Districts and natural resource agencies. Summer soil and water positions include wetland and watercourse inventories, field surveys, groundwater monitoring, and educational programs. Full-year IPs include GIS mapping, species inventory, invasive species management, and water quality monitoring at agencies like MN DNR, USFS, and nonprofit partners. Strong match for Erin’s GIS, water quality, and wildlife inventory skills. New positions post continuously at conservationcorps.org/join.

item-069.title: Biological Science Technician IP — Cherokee & Pisgah National Forests
item-069.org: Southeast Conservation Corps / US Forest Service · Eastern TN / Western NC
item-069.body: Southeast Conservation Corps regularly places AmeriCorps members with US Forest Service fisheries and wildlife teams in Cherokee National Forest (TN) and Pisgah National Forest (NC) — the exact landscape of Erin's Hurricane Helene research. item-069.desc: Southeast Conservation Corps regularly places AmeriCorps members with US Forest Service fisheries and wildlife teams in Cherokee National Forest (TN) and Pisgah National Forest (NC) — the exact landscape of Erin's Hurricane Helene research. Duties include aquatic resource monitoring, stream restoration, electrofishing, macroinvertebrate surveys, and freshwater snorkeling. This is a direct follow-on to her GEOL 423 (Contaminated Rivers) and ENVH 310 (Water Quality) coursework in the same geography.

item-072.title: USDA Forest Service Pathways Recent Graduate Program
item-072.org: USDA Forest Service · Multiple offices, SE and Mountain West
item-072.body: The USDA Forest Service Pathways Recent Graduate Program places graduates within the past 2 years in 1-year developmental positions that convert to permanent federal employment. Biological science, hydrology, GIS, and natural resources positions are available. Erin graduated May 2025 — eligible t...
item-072.desc: The USDA Forest Service Pathways Recent Graduate Program places graduates within the past 2 years in 1-year developmental positions that convert to permanent federal employment. Biological science, hydrology, GIS, and natural resources positions are available. Erin graduated May 2025 — eligible through May 2027. This is a direct federal career pathway without the competitive hurdle of the standard hiring process. Search USAJobs for "Pathways Recent Graduate USDA Forest Service" filtered by biological science or natural resources series.

item-058.title: Entry-Level Environmental Scientist — SE Region
item-058.org: Tetra Tech / AECOM / Geosyntec · Raleigh NC, Asheville NC, Charleston SC, Atlanta GA
item-058.body: Tetra Tech has an active Entry-Level Environmental Scientist posting for southeastern US (Aiken, SC area) focused on environmental permitting and regulatory compliance, with wetland delineation experience as a plus. AECOM is recruiting for an entry-level Environmental Scientist in GA, AL, FL, and...
item-058.desc: Tetra Tech has an active Entry-Level Environmental Scientist posting for southeastern US (Aiken, SC area) focused on environmental permitting and regulatory compliance, with wetland delineation experience as a plus. AECOM is recruiting for an entry-level Environmental Scientist in GA, AL, FL, and SC starting spring/summer 2026 — an Aug/Sep start for a qualified candidate is feasible. Geosyntec has openings in Asheville, NC specifically. All hire on rolling basis throughout the year.

item-094.title: Colorado State University — Funded MS, Mesocarnivore Ecology (Gerber Lab)
item-094.org: Fort Collins, CO · Dept. of Fish, Wildlife, & Conservation Biology
item-094.deadline: Mar 1, 2026 priority (passed) — next cycle ~Mar 2027 (Fall 2027 start); may inquire now
item-094.body: Funded MS assistantship with Dr. Brian D. Gerber on mesocarnivore (small carnivore) ecology — student develops a project + sampling frame and leads field surveys. $3,000/mo stipend + tuition + fees + health. The Mar 1, 2026 deadline has passed; watch/inquire for Fall 2027.
item-094.desc: Dr. Brian D. Gerber’s lab (Colorado State University, Dept. of Fish, Wildlife & Conservation Biology) offers a funded MS assistantship in mesocarnivore ecology. The student develops a project proposal and sampling frame in year one and leads field surveys — a strong match for Erin’s mammalogy and wildlife-management coursework. Funding: $3,000/month stipend + tuition + fees + health insurance, Fall 2026–Spring 2029. The March 1, 2026 application deadline for Fall 2026 has passed, so this is flagged for the next cycle (~March 2027 for Fall 2027 start). A brief, well-targeted inquiry email to Dr. Gerber now (subject "MS mesocarnivore", with cover letter, CV with 3–4 references, and unofficial BS transcripts) establishes contact early.

item-103.title: Environmental Restoration Field Technician — wetland & habitat restoration crew
item-103.org: Riparia Environmental (MacKay Sposito subsidiary) · Fife, WA
item-103.body: Seasonal Pacific Northwest field tech role doing wetland and upland restoration — native plantings, invasive/noxious weed control (including herbicide app), and site upkeep across WA/OR/ID/CA projects.
item-103.desc: A hands-on entry-level seasonal role with a regional environmental consultancy — solid resume-builder for restoration ecology and a way to break into PNW work. Pay is $22–$26/hr depending on experience, and full-time employees get benefits (medical/dental/vision, 401k match, PTO). Labor-intensive: bending, squatting, carrying 30–40 lb loads (up to 90 occasional). Good fit for Erin's restoration ecology and wetlands interests, and a route into the West Coast region. Apply through Riparia's career page; entry-level (0–1 yr) acceptable.

item-109.title: Louisiana State University — Funded PhD, Conservation Ecology (Entomology)
item-109.org: Baton Rouge, LA · Department of Entomology
item-109.body: Funded PhD in LSU's Entomology Dept with a conservation-ecology focus — assistantship $30,667/yr with non-resident tuition waiver and standard benefits.
item-109.desc: Posted on the Texas A&M Natural Resources Job Board in early June 2026. Although housed in Entomology, the project is conservation-ecology framed — good for Erin if she's open to insect-pollinator or aquatic-insect angles on ecosystem health (a real growth area in EJ/restoration work). LSU's Baton Rouge programs give her another Southeast option to pair with the LSU WABL/Coastal records she's already considering. Reach out to potential advisors before applying — funding is tied to specific faculty.
item-109.badge: Reach / review — verify specific advisor + project fit before applying

item-117.title: SUNY-ESF — Funded MS/PhD, Fish & Wetland Ecology (Arsenault & Farrell)
item-117.org: Syracuse, NY · Dept. of Environmental Biology / Aquatic & Fisheries Science
item-117.deadline: Rolling — contact PIs first; SUNY-ESF official grad deadline Jan 15, 2027 for Fall 2027
item-117.body: Fully funded MS or PhD co-advised by Dr. Emily Arsenault and Dr. John Farrell, studying how seasonal hydroperiod shapes energy flow and food webs in wetlands used by juvenile Northern Pike (St. Lawrence River system). Skills built: stable isotope analysis, otolith microchemistry, fish & wetland ecology.
item-117.desc: Combines wetland hydrology with fisheries — exactly Erin's intersecting interests. Field season May-Oct at Thousand Islands & Cranberry Lake biological stations; academic year in Syracuse. New NY Sea Grant funded ($217k) so resources are fresh. Bachelor's-direct PhD or MS both open. Email both PIs with CV + statement of interest before applying through the grad school.

item-092.title: Texas A&M University–Kingsville — Funded MS, Watershed Restoration (Xi Lab)
item-092.body: Funded MS in watershed restoration with Dr. Weimin Xi (Inflation Reduction Act Urban & Community Forestry grant): field surveys, statistical and spatial (GIS) analyses, forest/rangeland restoration. Stipend + out-of-state tuition waiver. BS in Bio/Forestry/Ecology/Env Sci/GIS or related. Apply by emailing Dr. Xi a single PDF: letter of interest, CV, transcripts, 3 references.
item-092.desc: Dr. Weimin Xi’s lab at Texas A&M University–Kingsville is recruiting a funded MS student in ecological restoration of degraded watersheds and ecosystems, supported by an Inflation Reduction Act Urban & Community Forestry Program grant. The position runs field surveys plus statistical and spatial (GIS / geospatial) analyses related to forest and rangeland restoration — a direct match for Erin’s watershed, GIS, and field-ecology skills. Funding: stipend + out-of-state tuition waiver. Start: September 2026. Qualifications: BS in Biology, Forestry, Ecology, Botany, Environmental Science, Geography, GIS, or related. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled; apply by emailing Dr. Xi (weimin.xi@tamuk.edu) a single PDF with letter of interest, CV, unofficial transcripts, and three academic/research references. Lab: drxilab.netlify.app

item-116.title: Texas A&M Natural Resources Institute — Funded MS/PhD, Freshwater Mussels & Water Quality (Randklev & Lopez)
item-116.org: College Station, TX · Rangeland, Wildlife & Fisheries Mgmt
item-116.deadline: Rolling — Summer/Fall 2026 or Spring 2027 starts; apply now
item-116.body: Fully funded assistantships in Dr. Charles Randklev & Dr. Roel Lopez's freshwater mussel ecology group. PhD focuses on how water quality drives mussel growth/survival in Trinity & central TX rivers; MS focuses on field surveys across east/central Texas. PhD ~$35k/yr × 4 yrs; MS ~$32k/yr × 2 yrs (stipend + tuition).
item-116.desc: Mussels are sentinel taxa for the exact kind of stream-quality work Erin did on the Pigeon River. The MS track (field-survey heavy) is the better fit — bachelor's + interest sufficient, no MS prerequisite. Apply by emailing a single PDF (cover letter + 3 references) to BOTH PIs. Texas A&M NRI is a top-tier shop with strong industry pipeline.

item-006.title: Clemson University — Elmore Lab, Bird Response to Helene
item-006.org: Clemson, SC · Dept. of Forestry & Environmental Conservation
item-006.body: The Elmore Lab at Clemson's Forestry & Environmental Conservation dept. was recruiting MS and PhD students for a Hurricane Helene bird ecology project. MS candidate to coordinate nest monitoring studying how priority bird species (Kentucky Warbler, Golden-winged Warbler, Cerulean Warbler, Swainso...
item-006.desc: The Elmore Lab at Clemson's Forestry & Environmental Conservation dept. was recruiting MS and PhD students for a Hurricane Helene bird ecology project. MS candidate to coordinate nest monitoring studying how priority bird species (Kentucky Warbler, Golden-winged Warbler, Cerulean Warbler, Swainson's Warbler, Ruffed Grouse) respond to hurricane damage. MS stipend $30k/yr; PhD $35k/yr. Field work in Pisgah National Forest. Verify if still open.

item-130.title: Eastern Illinois University — Funded MS, Fisheries & Aquatic Ecology (Wabash River)
item-130.org: Charleston, IL · Center for Fisheries & Aquatic Sciences
item-130.deadline: Apply by August 19, 2026 (review began Nov 25, 2025; open until filled)
item-130.body: Up to four funded MS research assistantships at EIU's Center for Fisheries & Aquatic Sciences — $1,600/month stipend plus a full tuition waiver. Thesis projects include Wabash River fish community assessment, Channel Catfish demographics and spawning-box evaluation in small impoundments, and invasive carp reproduction, recruitment, and movement ecology.
item-130.desc: Listed on the Texas A&M Natural Resources Job Board. A strong, BS-eligible route into a funded fisheries/aquatic-ecology MS — directly relevant to Erin's water-quality and watershed background (her Pigeon River trace-metal capstone), and her trapping and camera/field-monitoring skills transfer well to fish-community and invasive-species work. Recent-graduate friendly (unofficial transcripts accepted); apply early since review is rolling and the spots fill. Email a cover letter, CV with GPA, transcripts, and three references to Dr. Daniel Roth (drroth@eiu.edu).

item-124.title: USFWS Inventory & Monitoring Conservation Planning Fellow — Southeast Region
item-124.org: American Conservation Experience (ACE) EPIC / AmeriCorps · USFWS Southeast Region (remote, SE preference)
item-124.deadline: Rolling — verify current Southeast posting on the ACE EPIC board
item-124.body: AmeriCorps individual placement with USFWS Inventory & Monitoring: GIS/ArcGIS Pro data management, maps, and reports supporting refuge and ecological-services work across the Southeast Region. ~$700/week living allowance; gear reimbursement; confers federal hiring authority after 640 hours.
item-124.desc: Strong fit and a direct USFWS on-ramp — ArcGIS-based monitoring in Erin's home region (NC/SC/GA/FL/AL/TN/KY/AR/LA/MS) with federal hiring authority that advances her USFWS goal. ⚠ Verify a current SE-region posting: ACE EPIC rotates these on a rolling basis, so the durable entry point is the ACE EPIC job map (saved search recommended).

item-126.title: Appalachian Conservation Corps — Individual Placement (Natural Resource Management)
item-126.org: Appalachian Conservation Corps (Conservation Legacy) / AmeriCorps · VA / WV / Mid-Atlantic host sites
item-126.deadline: Rolling — postings appear on the open-positions board
item-126.body: AmeriCorps individual placements with agencies and nonprofits across the central Appalachians: natural-resource management, restoration, monitoring, and (for some roles) GIS. Living allowance plus Segal Education Award; many placements confer Public Lands Corps federal hiring authority.
item-126.desc: Good fit close to Erin's WCU/Pigeon River base, in Appalachian ecosystems she already knows. The Public Lands Corps hiring authority is a real federal-track lever. Submit a résumé to the recruiter to be matched to rotating placements.

item-125.title: River Corps Member — watershed restoration & water-quality monitoring
item-125.org: River Science (RiverCorps) / AmeriCorps · Statewide Colorado host sites
item-125.deadline: Rolling — verify next intake (2026 cohort underway)
item-125.body: AmeriCorps program placing members at Colorado watershed organizations and agencies for low-tech process-based restoration, hydrology and water-quality monitoring, and GIS. Living allowance ~$17,500 plus Segal Education Award; state-accredited hydrology & water-quality monitoring certifications.
item-125.desc: Good-to-strong fit: restoration + water-quality sampling + GIS mirrors Erin's Pigeon River trace-metal/sediment work, with field certifications that build her résumé. ⚠ The 2026 cohort already started — confirm mid-cycle or 2027 openings via the member interest form.

item-127.title: Big Sky Watershed Corps Member — hydrology, GIS & watershed coordination
item-127.org: Montana Conservation Corps + MT watershed partners / AmeriCorps · Statewide Montana host sites
item-127.deadline: 2026 cohort closed — recruitment for the next term opens ~August 2026
item-127.body: AmeriCorps program placing members with Montana conservation districts, tribes, agencies, and watershed nonprofits for hydrologic field techniques, GIS, and watershed coordination. ~$1,200 biweekly, Segal Education Award, free health insurance. Bachelor's in natural resources preferred.
item-127.desc: Strong fit and an ideal grad-school/agency springboard combining hydrology fieldwork + GIS + watershed coordination — Erin clears the bachelor's-preferred profile cleanly. Timing: this cycle is closed, so set an August 2026 reminder to apply for the next term.

item-070.title: Wildlife Monitoring IP — Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge (2026 cycle)
item-070.org: American Youthworks / USFWS · Fort Sill / Lawton, OK
item-070.deadline: March 2, 2026 – November 6, 2026 (confirmed active) — check American Youthworks for backfill
item-070.body: American Youthworks places AmeriCorps members at the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge and Fort Sill through the ARTES (At Risk, Threatened, and Endangered Species) Program — monitoring tricolored bat, monarch butterfly, black-capped vireo, and northern bobwhite quail. The 2026 cycle (March 2 – N...
item-070.desc: American Youthworks places AmeriCorps members at the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge and Fort Sill through the ARTES (At Risk, Threatened, and Endangered Species) Program — monitoring tricolored bat, monarch butterfly, black-capped vireo, and northern bobwhite quail. The 2026 cycle (March 2 – Nov 6) had a January 25 deadline; the 2026–27 version will follow a similar timeline. 1,200-hour term provides full Segal education award (~$7,395). $600/week living allowance + $225/week housing stipend.

item-135.title: Montana Conservation Corps — Open AmeriCorps Positions (source)
item-135.org: Montana Conservation Corps (AmeriCorps) · Bozeman, Kalispell & statewide MT host sites
item-135.deadline: Rolling — roles post on the MCC open-positions board; many 2026 roles fill early, so set a "Get Notified for 2027" alert
item-135.start: Varies by role (e.g., Fall Wildland Restoration term Aug 3 – Oct 16, 2026)
item-135.body: Montana Conservation Corps runs AmeriCorps field crews and individual placements across Montana and the Northern Rockies — wildland restoration, trail and habitat work, and natural-resource projects with federal and tribal land partners. Roles carry a living stipend plus a Segal Education Award; longer terms include health insurance. This is the recurring SOURCE board (postings rotate); the Fall-only Wildland Restoration Team Member (Bozeman/Kalispell) lists a $1,200 bi-weekly living stipend and a $1,565.08 education award.
item-135.desc: A durable entry point into Mountain West conservation service. MCC crews give Erin Northern Rockies field experience and Public Lands Corps federal hiring authority — a strong complement to her Southeast/Appalachian background and her USFWS goal. Because individual postings open and close throughout the year, save this board and use the "Get Notified" sign-up rather than chasing single listings; apply early since many 2026 roles have already closed.

materials.title: Cover Letter Service Corps Base for Sustainability
materials.content:
June 15, 2026

Re: Restoration Crew Member

To whom it may concern:

I would like to apply for the Restoration Crew Member position with ECC because the position involves placement on wetlands restoration, coastal/watershed monitoring, and invasive-species removal projects across the Lowcountry. My undergraduate experience aligns well with the kind of applied water-quality and sediment work this role does day-to-day. My previous experience with AmeriCorps NCCC included invasive species removal, proper use of forestry equipment, and trail maintenance. As I look ahead to an eventual graduate degree, I feel this is a valuable opportunity into more permanent conservation work.  

I am a recent graduate of Western Carolina University (BS Environmental Science, May 2025, Magna Cum Laude, 3.731 GPA). I have hands-on field experience and a year of AmeriCorps NCCC service, and I am again ready to commit to a structured service term with a conservation organization.

My undergraduate field experience includes wetland delineation using the Army Corps manual, small mammal trapping and tagging, camera trap monitoring with Wildlife Insights, and a trace metal analysis in the Pigeon River Basin on Hurricane Helene’s sediment redistribution. I am comfortable with extended field work — multi-day trips in remote areas, physical labor in variable weather, and the close-quarters teamwork that AmeriCorps work demands.

I have worked in disaster-affected landscapes, both as a volunteer in Hurricane Helene relief and as a researcher documenting the storm’s downstream effects on the Pigeon River. Lowcountry restoration work would let me apply that experience in a structured, longer-term capacity, with the salt marsh and oyster reef systems being a productive complement to the freshwater wetland work I have done.

I’m willing to relocate, complete a full term, and contribute meaningfully to your crew or placement. Please let me know if there is further information needed.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Erin Lamberton
